newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Laws sets out NZ First bottom lines.
newsitem.headline: Laws sets out NZ First bottom lines.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters' former right-hand man Michael Laws has set out what he sees as the bottom lines for the party to enter a coalition government.
Writing in the Evening Post newspaper on Friday, Laws said New Zealand First had only one chance to make an impact before becoming a junior partner in a new government.
"Far from having a position of great influence and importance, NZ First's position is actually very weak. It has but one card and one card only.
"After that NZ First is essentially rendered as a political bystander, its fortunes dependent on its older, bigger and more cynical spouse," Laws said.

New Zealand First holds the balance of power after the October 12 general election and is negotiating with both the main opposition Labour party and the caretaker governing National party over the shape of the new administration. Laws resigned from politics shortly after the election but had a significant input into the party's policy.

Laws said New Zealand First should insist on policy bottom lines costing about $750 million a year, including scrapping the superannuation surcharge, free doctors visits for under-12-year-olds, greater spending on childhood education, its $150 million employment policy and a boost to police numbers.

But he said significant parliamentary reform would be the tangible and ongoing proof that New Zealand First had made a change to the political process and would be remembered long after one-off policy gains.
"Without that proof, NZ First's future is very shaky indeed." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
